Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt

Class Capabilities

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt.Capabilities
public final class Capabilities extends Object
What a script is allowed to do, decided by the host rather than by the script.

Mandela runs inside a desktop that also runs the user's files, so an unbounded eval is not acceptable anywhere except the CLI. The answer is not a bytecode verifier — the language has no unprivileged-mode split and adding one would double the machine — but an explicit grant list that every side-effecting built-in and host function consults before it acts. A script cannot widen its own capabilities: the object is handed to the Runtime and never exposed as a value.

Four shapes cover the users:

  • open() — the CLI and mandela repl: the real filesystem, the terminal, generous limits.
  • console() — a snippet a host pasted in: a console and nothing else, which is what Espresso's Run executes the current buffer under.
  • desktop(java.nio.file.Path) — a panel, widget or app script: files under one directory, a console, the clock, no JVM types, no sockets.
  • webPage() — a script embedded in the Web Browser: nothing but computing, its own console channel and a small step budget, because page content is untrusted by definition.

Limits are enforced by the machine itself: a runaway loop and unbounded recursion both stop with a catchable LimitError that quotes the ceiling they hit, so a mistyped loop { } cannot hang the desktop.

    • console

      public static Capabilities console()
      The mode for a snippet a host pasted in: a console and nothing else.

      Files, the environment, sockets, threads, processes and JVM types are all refused, so the default an embedding API hands out is the safe one and a host has to say so on purpose to get anything more. This is what Mandela.engine() and the JSR-223 engine start from; open() is the opposite end and belongs to a command line run by the person who wrote the script.

      Returns:
      stdout and stderr, with a modest budget

    • resolve

      public Path resolve(String requested, String what)
      Resolves a script-supplied path inside the granted root.

      Every file built-in goes through here, so "../" and absolute paths cannot escape the directory the host handed over.

      Parameters:
      requested - the path the script asked for
      what - a short description for the error message
      Returns:
      the resolved, confined path
      Throws:
      MandelaError - when the result would fall outside the root
